author: Surbhi Jain
title: Walmart Is Winning Thanksgiving. Is Target Losing the Holiday Shopping Battle?
teaser: Walmart's $35 Thanksgiving meal for 10 undercuts Target on a per-person basis. Here's what the holiday price war means for retail stocks.
body:
Walmart Inc. (NASDAQ:WMT) is making Thanksgiving dinner a $3.50-per-person proposition. Target Corp (NYSE:TGT) is offering a $5-per-person meal. That gap captures a fight among retailers: winning shoppers watching every dollar without giving up holiday traditions that bring them into stores.

Walmart’s $35 meal for 10 is down from $39.93 last year and includes 18% more individual items, according to Axios. Target is advertising a $30 meal for six, keeping its price unchanged for a second year, according to NBC News. On a per-person basis, Walmart’s offer is 30% cheaper.

Walmart Makes Value the Main Event

Thanksgiving baskets are more than seasonal promotions. They are a visible test of how far a retailer can stretch a household’s budget — and a reason to choose one store for the rest of the shopping list.

Walmart is leaning into that proposition with a one-click basket built around a turkey, sides and pumpkin pie. Aldi is advertising a meal for 10 for under $39, although its basket has fewer items than last year’s.

Costco Wholesale Corp (NASDAQ:COST) is taking a different tack: its prepared Thanksgiving dinner costs $199.99 for eight, unchanged from 2025, and is positioned as a ready-to-serve option.

Kroger Co (NYSE:KR) has moved away from a fixed-price meal bundle, instead promoting individual discounts and prepared foods in different portion sizes.

That leaves Walmart competing on price, convenience and the perception of getting more for less.

The Margin Trade-Off

There is a catch for investors. Retailers may sacrifice profit on holiday staples to get shoppers through the door, hoping they add snacks, drinks and other groceries to their carts.

Wholesale frozen turkey prices were up 12% year over year as of Nov. 9, reported Reuters, while wholesale russet potato prices had climbed about 46%. Retailers have kept consumer prices comparatively restrained, absorbing some pressure to reinforce their value message.

Read Also: Grocers Keep Thanksgiving Meals Cheap as Turkey Costs Rise

Walmart’s scale and grocery reach make its aggressive pricing important to watch. Target’s offer is cheaper in total dollars, but serves fewer people; Costco is selling convenience rather than the lowest cost per guest. Kroger’s flexible approach may appeal to shoppers who want to build their own meal.

Why it Matters

One Thanksgiving promotion cannot determine which retailer is winning the holiday season. But the offers show how differently these chains are positioning themselves as affordability remains a consumer concern.

Investors should watch comparable-sales results, grocery traffic and management commentary on promotions and margins. If Walmart’s basket brings shoppers back for more than turkey, it could strengthen its competitive position. For Target, the test is whether its value offer translates into broader store traffic — not simply whether it can match Walmart’s price per person.

author: Surbhi Jain
title: Intel Stock Is on the Verge of a Death Cross. Is Its Comeback Already in Trouble?
teaser: Intel stock nears a Death Cross as AI growth and new customer wins struggle to restore confidence in its turnaround.
body:
Intel Corp (NASDAQ:INTC) has some signs that its comeback is gaining traction: data-center revenue is surging, an outside customer has signed on for its advanced manufacturing process, and Microsoft Corp (NASDAQ:MSFT) has chosen its packaging technology for Azure chips.

Yet the stock is telling a different story. A bearish technical signal is just cents away, putting the market’s faith in the turnaround under scrutiny.

A Death Cross Is Near

Chart created using Benzinga Pro

Intel shares trade around $54.47, below their eight-day and 20-day moving averages of $55.15 and $59.36. More importantly, the 50-day average is $87.70, barely above the 200-day average at $87.66. The four-cent gap puts the stock on the verge of a Death Cross, which occurs when the 50-day average falls below the 200-day.

The setup reflects Intel’s recent decline, but it is not confirmation yet. The 14-day relative strength index is 35.93, signaling weakness without reaching the conventional oversold threshold of 30. The MACD (moving average convergence/divergence) indicator remains below zero, although its positive histogram reading of 1.15 suggests selling momentum may be easing. A rebound could still delay the crossover.

Read Also: Intel Just Took 14A Off Death Row — The 2028 Clock Is Ticking

The Comeback Has Real Progress

There are reasons investors might resist writing off the recovery. Third-quarter revenue rose 21% year over year to $16.5 billion, while Data Center and AI revenue grew 78% to $7.32 billion. CEO Lip-Bu Tan said demand for Intel CPUs remains robust and called Xeon demand "extraordinary," while identifying additional supply as an immediate priority.

Intel also secured its first external customer for its 18A-P manufacturing process, although it has not disclosed the customer’s identity.

Separately, Microsoft became the first publicly named customer for Intel Foundry’s EMIB packaging technology for Azure silicon, alongside a multiyear Xeon supply agreement. These are meaningful endorsements, but not yet proof of a profitable foundry business at scale.

The Market Still Wants Proof

The counterweight is Intel’s uneven outlook. Client Computing revenue fell 5% to $8.1 billion in the third quarter, and management expects the PC slowdown to persist through at least the first half of 2027.

Intel forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion. Its foundry segment also posted a $1.9 billion operating loss, while external revenue was only $411 million.

Investment Takeaway

The approaching Death Cross does not prove Intel’s turnaround has failed; moving averages are lagging indicators, and the MACD histogram hints that selling pressure could be cooling.

But the chart captures the burden facing Tan: turn customer wins and AI demand into consistent shipments, stronger foundry economics and better guidance. Until investors see that, good news may struggle to repair confidence.

title: Situational Awareness Lost 65% in Q3, Investor Leopold Aschenbrenner Warns Nvidia, Microsoft, Tesla Could Lose Their Edge: Report
teaser: Leopold Aschenbrenner's AI hedge fund lost 65% in Q3 after an AI selloff, prompting tighter risk controls and portfolio changes.
body:
Leopold Aschenbrenner’s Situational Awareness hedge fund reportedly lost 65% after fees in the third quarter, exposing the risks of leveraged AI trades even as the fund remained sharply higher for the year.

Aschenbrenner disclosed the loss in an investor letter seen by the Wall Street Journal on Wednesday. The fund nearly unraveled in July after an AI selloff hit its borrowing-fueled positions.

Situational Awareness remained up 88.5% through September. Aschenbrenner said the firm restructured its portfolio and is hiring an experienced chief risk officer after acknowledging mistakes made during the fund’s turbulent period.

"Many of our predictions — which seemed like science fiction two years ago — came true. And yet we also learned how wrong we could be, and how merciless the market is when we are," Aschenbrenner wrote.

He expects the fund could eventually resume short selling and use borrowed money again, but at lower levels. Its revised risk framework, he said, must reflect the extreme volatility associated with developing advanced AI systems.

Aschenbrenner said the fund will accept market volatility but avoid investments that carry “existential risk”, even if its analysis proves wrong.

Situational Awareness did not immediately respond to Benzinga’s request for comments.

Read Also: $65 Billion in AI Exposure: Why CalPERS Takes a Closer Look at Big Tech

AI Risks Challenge Tech Giants’ Moats

Aschenbrenner also warned that superintelligent AI could weaken the competitive advantages of Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA), Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (NASDAQ:AMD), Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ:MSFT), Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL), Tesla Inc. (NASDAQ:TSLA) and Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ:SPCX)

The investor called the market pullback "radical," arguing that AI valuations now imply modest growth for leading AI labs, despite his forecast that their combined revenue run-rate will exceed $1 trillion by the end of 2027.

Aschenbrenner Explores Fund Relaunch

The reported losses have continued to shape the fund’s future. Four months after the steep decline and emergency assistance following the July sell-off, Aschenbrenner has reportedly held discussions with prime brokers and investors about a possible "Situational Awareness 2.0" relaunch.

The discussions came amid attention ahead of Anthropic PBC (NASDAQ:ANT) initial public offering (IPO). Aschenbrenner has reportedly been trying to reassure investors and banks that stronger risk controls will prevent further AI-related losses. He is also exploring new outside funding, though plans for leverage, fundraising and the fund’s structure remain undecided.

title: EXCLUSIVE: Black Friday Could Outperform Cyber Monday as AI Memory Crunch Pushes Up Prices, Says Louis Navellier — Experts List Top 5 Stocks to Watch
teaser: Louis Navellier expects stronger Black Friday sales but warns high memory prices could hurt Cyber Monday. Walmart, Target, Best Buy in focus.
body:
Veteran investor Louis Navellier expects Black Friday sales to outperform Cyber Monday, warning that high memory prices could hurt the latter. Walmart Inc. (NASDAQ:WMT), Target Corp. (NYSE:TGT) and Best Buy Co. Inc. (NYSE:BBY) are among the retail stocks in focus.

Navellier Flags Cyber Monday Risks

"Due to high memory prices, I suspect that Cyber Monday may be a bust," Navellier told Benzinga.

"However, consumers seem to be in a good mood, so Black Friday’s sales should be better," he added.

His comments suggest contrasting expectations for the two shopping events, with Black Friday scheduled for Nov. 27 and Cyber Monday for Nov. 30.

Read Also: Is The Stock Market Open on Thanksgiving 2026? Here’s When Trading Resumes on Black Friday

Experts Warn Higher Spending May Mask Consumer Weakness

Alex Tsepaev, chief strategy officer at B2PRIME Group, warned that higher holiday spending might not indicate stronger consumer demand.

"It’s possible that goods have simply become more expensive, so spending more doesn’t necessarily mean buying more," Tsepaev said.

He recommended tracking purchase volumes, average transaction values and credit card debt to determine whether consumers are purchasing more products or relying on borrowing.

Tsepaev warned that increased credit dependence could leave households vulnerable to another economic downturn.

Dean Chen, an analyst at Bitunix, echoed those concerns, describing the U.S. consumer landscape as "K-shaped."

Chen said higher-income households retain relatively strong spending power, while lower-income consumers increasingly seek discounts, switch to private-label products and rely on credit.

He recommended examining transaction volumes, discount levels, and buy-now-pay-later usage rather than relying solely on headline sales figures.

Defensive Stocks Draw Attention

Rather than pursuing short-term holiday sales growth, Chen favored companies with stable cash flows, limited financial leverage, and reasonable valuations.

He identified PepsiCo Inc. (NASDAQ:PEP) and Procter & Gamble Co. (NYSE:PG) as companies worth monitoring because of their exposure to everyday consumer necessities.

However, Chen cautioned that rising costs, consumers switching to cheaper alternatives, and excessive valuations could still threaten defensive stocks.

author: Tanya Rawat
title: Chuck Schumer Says Trump’s SNAP Cuts, Tariffs Force Americans Into ‘Impossible Choices’ at Thanksgiving as Jacky Rosen Slams ‘Reckless Economic Policies’
teaser: Democrats warn Thanksgiving affordability is under pressure, citing grocery costs, tariffs and proposed food assistance cuts.
body:
Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) said Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) cuts and tariff policies backed by President Donald Trump and Republicans have forced Americans to make “impossible choices” at Thanksgiving, as other Democrats also criticized rising food costs.

Schumer made the remarks in a post on X on Thursday, saying that “Thanksgiving should be a time for families to gather, rest, and break bread with loved ones,” Schumer wrote. “But devastating SNAP cuts and reckless tariff policies brought by Trump and the GOP have forced Americans to make impossible choices.” He added: “The American people deserve better and our Democratic majority is on the way to help.”

Reich Calls Tax Cuts and Aid Cuts a ‘Policy Choice’

Former Labor Secretary Robert Reich also posted on X on Thursday: “Billionaire tax cuts are a policy choice. Cutting healthcare for millions is a policy choice. Cutting food assistance for children is a policy choice. Taking from the poor and giving to the rich is a policy choice.” Reich added that “it does not have to be like this.”

Read Also: Mark Cuban Warns Healthcare Usage Could ‘Explode’ Under Medicare for All as US Lacks Enough Doctors, Nurses: ‘Plan for the Worst’

Rosen, Goodlander Cite Food Costs and SNAP

Senator Jacky Rosen (D-NV)  wrote families gathering for Thanksgiving are facing higher grocery bills alongside rising costs for gas, health care and housing, leaving household budgets squeezed from multiple directions. Blaming Trump’s “reckless economic policies” for the added pressure, she said she would continue working to lower food costs for Nevadans, including by passing legislation to exempt grocery products from Trump’s tariffs and reversing Republican cuts to the SNAP.

Rep. Maggie Goodlander (D-NH) tied the spirit of Thanksgiving to concerns over food affordability, saying families gathering to break bread with loved ones are already feeling the squeeze of grocery bills. She warned that a new Trump administration proposal could cut off food assistance for about 15,000 Granite Staters, including 6,000 children, and said she is pressing the administration to reverse course. Goodlander also urged people to weigh in, noting that public comments on the proposal remain open until Dec. 10.

Schumer Previously Pointed to Price Increases and SNAP Removals

Schumer raised the same themes in a previous November post on X, where he blamed Trump’s war, tariffs and trade dispute with Canada for rising Thanksgiving grocery costs. He cited year-over-year increases of 36% for green beans, 26% for frozen turkey, more than 10% for yams and more than 8% for stuffing, and said 5.5 million Americans had been removed from SNAP, with another 6 million at risk of losing support.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture estimated that about 6.3 million people could lose SNAP eligibility by fiscal 2029 if a proposal restricting automatic eligibility for some recipients of the Temporary Assistance for Needy Families program took effect, in addition to 5.5 million who lost benefits over the previous year. Separately, under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, states’ share of SNAP administrative costs rose from 50% to 75% on Oct. 1.

Rollins Points to Easing Food Inflation

Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins said in a Wednesday post on X that food inflation is decreasing and that grocery stores are offering affordable Thanksgiving meal deals. She said on Newsmax that  Walmart Inc. (NASDAQ:WMT), Aldi, and other chains are offering meal deals at about $3 per person. The U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Economic Research Service, in its November Food Price Outlook released Tuesday, forecast grocery prices to rise 2.4% on average in 2026.

author: Mohd Haider
title: Trump to Attend TSMC Arizona Chip Plant Groundbreaking as Chipmaker's US Investment Expands: Report
teaser: TSMC shares gain attention as Trump prepares to attend the groundbreaking of its latest Arizona chip foundry on December 4.
body:
President Donald Trump will speak at the groundbreaking of a new Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (NYSE:TSM) chip foundry in Arizona on Dec. 4, as AI demand drives the company’s pledged $265 billion U.S. buildout.

The White House and TSMC confirmed the visit, the Associated Press reported on Wednesday. The event marks the start of construction on the fifth phase of the company’s Phoenix-area expansion.

The White House and TSMC did not immediately respond to Benzinga’s request for comments.

AI Demand Fuels U.S. Chipmaking Investment

TSMC makes chips in Arizona for Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA), Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL), Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (NASDAQ:AMD), Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ:AVGO) and Qualcomm Inc. (NASDAQ:QCOM).

In July, TSMC announced another $100 billion in U.S. manufacturing capacity. That brings its total pledged American investment to $265 billion.

Policy Credit and Jobs Impact

Trump has promoted the investments as a result of his tariffs. TSMC began Arizona construction under President Joe Biden. The bipartisan CHIPS and Science Act, which Biden signed, also provided some financial support.

According to the report, the White House said the expansion will create 10,000 direct jobs and 11,000 indirect jobs. The site currently supports more than 12,000 construction jobs.

The expansion comes as demand for AI chips continues to grow, while concerns about Taiwan’s dominance in chip manufacturing are also potentially driving the move.

Shares of TSMC closed 1.96% lower at $342.34 on Wednesday and were up 1.42% after hours.

title: ‘I’ve Never Seen Anything Like This’: Kevin O’Leary Admits Being ‘Wrong’ About Trump, Says He Underestimated President’s Push to Beat China in AI
teaser: Kevin O'Leary says he underestimated Trump's resolve to use executive power to make the U.S. an AI leader and beat China.
body:
Investor Kevin O’Leary acknowledged he had underestimated President Donald Trump’s willingness to intervene directly in corporate decisions to advance America’s artificial intelligence ambitions, saying the president is determined to keep the U.S. ahead of China in the technology race.

O’Leary Says Trump Is Prioritizing AI Dominance

On Wednesday, O’Leary shared a clip of his CNN interview on X, writing, “I’ve been investing for decades, and I’ve never seen anything like this.”

He added, “Trump has made it clear that winning the AI race against China is a priority. We’re seeing just how far-reaching that strategy is.”

In the interview, O’Leary admitted he had previously believed there was “zero” chance of the controversial decision being reversed, citing corporate governance and potential legal liabilities.

“I was wrong,” O’Leary said, acknowledging he had misread Trump’s priorities.

Trump Wants to Beat China In AI

O’Leary described the move as “unorthodox” and unprecedented, but argued it reflected the president’s broader strategy to establish U.S. leadership in AI, power generation and data centers.

“He wants to be number one against the Chinese in AI,” O’Leary said.

He added that Trump wants the U.S. to lead in energy infrastructure and data centers, warning that China remains America’s primary competitor.

“Either they win or we win,” O’Leary said, describing AI as a decisive contest for economic and national security leadership.

O’Leary acknowledged that investigations and corporate liabilities could follow the decision, but said scrutiny could ultimately clear the individual and company involved.

Read Also: Mark Kelly Sounds Alarm Over Suspected Chinese Spy’s Reported Access to NVDA CEO, Calls It a ‘Serious National Security Problem’

China’s AI Advances Raise Concerns Over US Leadership

Last week, recent warnings from business leaders highlighted the challenges facing America’s efforts to maintain AI dominance over China.

President Donald Trump’s push to reduce reliance on Chinese rare-earth supplies faced obstacles as Beijing continued to dominate processing and magnet manufacturing, leaving U.S. manufacturers, including Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL), Tesla Inc. (NASDAQ:TSLA), General Motors Co. (NYSE:GM) and Ford Motor Co. (NYSE:F), exposed to supply-chain disruptions.

Earlier this month, Palantir Technologies, Inc. (NASDAQ:PLTR) CEO Alex Karp called China a formidable AI rival, saying, “It is us or them,” and urged America and its allies to maintain technological leadership.

Last month, former Alphabet Inc.‘s (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL) Google CEO Eric Schmidt warned that China could still win the AI race through cheaper models, despite trailing the U.S. by about six months.

title: Microsoft Launches ‘Code Red’ After 24-Hour Outage, Wants Critical Fixes Deployed Worldwide in Just 1 Hour: Report (UPDATED)
teaser: Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ: MSFT) has reportedly launched its most urgent engineering response after a 24-hour outage disrupted major cloud services.
body:
Editor’s note: The story has been updated to include a comment from Microsoft.

Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ:MSFT) has reportedly launched its most urgent engineering response after a 24-hour outage disrupted major cloud services, targeting faster recovery, stronger safeguards and improved crisis coordination.

The software giant declared a "Code Red" overhaul after the disruption exposed weaknesses in its engineering and crisis-response systems, Reuters reported on Tuesday. The Code Red initiative introduces load shedding, geographic traffic partitioning and faster recovery protocols.

The outage affected Exchange Online, Outlook, Teams, Copilot and other Microsoft 365 products. Microsoft attributed the incident to an undetected Windows scalability defect introduced in July.

A Microsoft spokesperson said to Benzinga in an emailed statement that "Our work doesn’t end when service is restored. Our teams keep working around the clock to quickly implement any lessons learned, and our leadership makes sure this is our top priority. Our customers and partners depend on our services, and we owe it to them to not only fix problems when they occur, but to do everything we can to keep them from happening again."

Jason Henderson, president of Microsoft 365 Core, called the incident the most customer-impacting event in Exchange Online’s history, according to internal memos reviewed by the publication. Henderson said he would hold daily meetings with Microsoft’s Substrate leadership team and weekly reviews to monitor corrective actions following the outage.

Amanda Silver, a Microsoft corporate vice president, said responders exchanged more than 11,000 messages across 11 Teams chats while navigating fragmented diagnostic systems.

In another memo viewed by Reuters, Henderson said urgent patches for Microsoft 365 Core services are taking too long to deploy globally, citing one production fix that took five to six days to reach worldwide coverage. He said Microsoft needs to reduce the time from detecting critical security issues to safely deploying fixes worldwide to just one hour.

Read Also: Trump Floats Potential US Government Stake in Nvidia? 'Probably Not Too Late,' the President Says: 'Maybe I Should Do It'

Microsoft Outage Hits Wider Ecosystem

The November outage extended beyond workplace applications. An incident review cited disruptions involving Microsoft Defender for Office 365, Microsoft Defender XDR and Microsoft Purview, highlighting the breadth of the affected ecosystem.

During the incident, more than 130,000 Outlook complaints were recorded at the peak, while integrations used by OpenAI and Anthropic PBC (NASDAQ:ANT) were also affected. The outage underscored the reliance businesses place on Microsoft’s cloud infrastructure.

US Outages Raise Infrastructure Concerns

Earlier this month, a string of outages rocked the U.S. Besides Microsoft, other disruption events involved Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL), United Airlines Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ:UAL), JPMorgan Chase & Co. (NYSE:JPM) and the nationwide Federal Aviation Administration (FAA)-linked ground stop.

Jay Clayton, Director of National Intelligence, dismissed cyberattack concerns and warned that aging digital infrastructure requires major upgrades for AI performance and cybersecurity. He said modernization would bring inevitable disruptions. He said companies and government agencies should expect temporary disruptions during system upgrades and prepare for them proactively. 

Benzinga’s Edge Rankings place Microsoft in the 85th percentile for quality and the 97th percentile for growth, reflecting its strong performance in both areas.

Price Action: Year-to-date, MSFT shares have climbed 2.59%, as per Benzinga Pro. The stock was trading 2.99% lower at $481.30 premarket on Wednesday.

title: TruGolf (TRUG) Stock Climbs 19% After Hours: What's Driving the Surge?
teaser: TruGolf Holdings shares jump 18.94% in after-hours trading following a leadership shake-up and the appointment of three strategic advisors.
body:
TruGolf Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ:TRUG) climbed 18.94% to $0.31 in after-hours trading Wednesday, following a leadership shake-up.

TruGolf Names New Chairman, Adds Three Strategic Advisors

On Tuesday, the Utah-based golf technology and digital asset company said that Richard Dolan, Kevin Dent and Roger Premo joined as strategic advisors to the company and its subsidiary, Polymath Research Inc.

Dolan, a Toronto-based strategist with 30 years of experience in wealth management and real estate investment, will help bring issuers and real-world assets onto the Polymath platform. Dent will focus on building partnerships with technology, gaming, and entertainment platforms.

Dent previously worked in business development at Amazon.com Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) Web Services Game Tech. Premo formerly served as global head of strategy at International Business Machines Corp. (NYSE:IBM).

David Hackett, who joined the board when the Polymath acquisition closed on Oct. 8, succeeded Brenner Adams as chairman. Adams remains a director and interim CEO.

“Our board brings together public-market, capital-markets, and operating experience,” Adams said in the company’s press release.

title: EXCLUSIVE: Market Expert Likes What Greg Abel is Doing at Berkshire – ‘Alphabet Investment is Going to Pay Big Dividends’
teaser: Market expert Jay Woods is impressed with what Greg Abel has done at Berkshire Hathaway, particularly one investment.
body:
Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE:BRK)(NYSE:BRK) stock is beating the S&P 500 year-to-date by more than a 3x margin heading into Thanksgiving. Market expert Jay Woods told Benzinga that new Berkshire CEO Greg Abel is doing some great things as the successor to legendary investor Warren Buffett.

• Berkshire Hathaway stock is trading at elevated levels. Where are BRK-A shares going?

Jay Woods on Greg Abel

With big shoes to fill, Abel took over as Berkshire Hathaway CEO at the start of 2026.

"Abel’s done a couple interesting things. He traded UNH," Woods told Benzinga, recalling a trade in UnitedHealth Group (NYSE:UNH) stock. "He’s been allocating a little more aggressively to more opportunistic events. I find that fascinating."

Woods, who is the Freedom Capital Markets chief market strategist, said insurance stocks have done well, which could be part of the reason Berkshire Hathaway stock is up. Another reason could be bets on big technology names such as Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL).

"When they got into Apple, everyone said they were so late, but it was the best thing they ever did."

Woods said Alphabet is now the conglomerate’s second biggest tech investment outside of Apple Inc (NASDAQ:AAPL).

"I think that Google, or as it’s called Alphabet, investment is going to pay big dividends."

Woods is an investor in Alphabet stock and sees the company as a great AI play.  

Read Also: Berkshire Hathaway Takes Stake In AOL Owner Bending Spoons, Nearly Doubles Lennar Holding

Berkshire’s 2026 Success

Berkshire Hathaway stock is up 16.7% year-to-date as of Wednesday, outperforming the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE:SPY), which tracks the S&P 500 by more than three times. The SPY is currently up 5% year-to-date in 2026.

If the gains stay similar, this would mark a great first-year performance for Abel as CEO of the conglomerate, especially after Berkshire Hathaway trailed the S&P 500 in 2025.

Woods said there could be more big moves ahead too.

"Look at the cash. They haven’t done a deal in quite some time. So, Abel is sitting back," Woods said.

title: S&P 500 Pares Losses as Fed Beige Book Signals Optimism: 10 Tech Stocks Bouncing off Lows on Wednesday
teaser: S&P 500 pares losses as the Nasdaq 100 holds Friday's low. Most Fed districts expect growth, and QQQ, Arm and Nebius lead a tech rebound.
body:
Wall Street went back to the scene of Friday’s panic on Wednesday. This time, the floor held, and the selloff lost its grip.

The Nasdaq 100 sank as low as 24,970.66 in the first half hour of trading. That was roughly 60 points above the 24,910.48 intraday low it hit on Friday, Nov. 20.

From there, the index climbed 3.9% to 25,951 by 2 p.m. ET, trimming its daily loss to 1%.

The S&P 500 traveled the same road. After falling as much as 3.2% to 6,970.11, it recovered to 7,174.52, down just 0.4%.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average swung more than 1,300 points from its low and turned higher, adding 230 points, or 0.5%, to 50,249. The Russell 2000 rose 0.9% to 2,709.

Read Also: Nasdaq 100 Drops 2.5% on AI Credit Fears, Nvidia Sinks 7%: Stock Market Today

What Broke at the Open

Three blows landed in the first hour. First, credit. Worries about the debt behind the artificial-intelligence buildout returned, with five-year credit-default swaps on CoreWeave Inc. (NASDAQ:CRWV) at 13.3%, up from 4.47% at their June lows, according to FactSet data. Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) fell as much as 9.1% before paring the drop to 4.5% at $148.35.

Second, trade. The U.S. Trade Representative proposed new Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies, including up to 20% on China, 15% on the European Union, Japan, South Korea and Taiwan, 25% on India and 35% on Vietnam. Hearings start Jan. 25, 2027, so the duties are not immediate.

Third, inflation. Core PCE prices rose 3.3% from a year earlier in October, above the 3.2% forecast. At the same time, third-quarter GDP grew at a 4.3% annualized pace, well above the 3.5% estimate.

“The big highlight from this morning’s data is GDP, which at 4.3% shows that the economy is booming, but unfortunately the inflation data is still too high and is unlikely to convince the Fed to remain on hold,” Chris Zaccarelli, chief investment officer at Northlight Asset Management, said in emailed comments.

Why the Nasdaq 100 Retest Matters

Friday’s low was not a random number. The Nasdaq 100 dropped 5.6% that day, then surged 6.9% on Monday after Jensen Huang‘s return to Nvidia, before giving back 2% on Tuesday.

Wednesday was the first real test of that bottom. When an index returns to a recent low and bounces before breaking it, chart watchers call it a higher low, often an early sign that sellers are tiring.

The Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) rose 4.3% from its morning low. The VanEck Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SMH) did better, climbing 6.8% off its trough.

Still, the Nasdaq 100 remains down 8.6% in November.

The Beige Book Brings a Steadier Read

The Federal Reserve’s Beige Book landed at 2 p.m. ET, with most of the rebound already in place, and did not derail it.

Eight of the 12 Fed districts reported slight to moderate growth, while four reported no change, a touch softer than October’s nine. However, the outlook was firmer. “Overall, the majority of Districts expected slight to moderate growth,” the report said.

Employment rose slightly, mostly through replacement hiring, and prices rose moderately as firms cited tariff-related expenses. Data center-related imports also rose.

Bonds rallied. The 10-year Treasury yield fell 9 basis points to 4.84%, the 2-year yield dropped 5 basis points to 4.63% and the 30-year yield declined 9 basis points to 5.23%.

Gold was flat at $3,557 an ounce, silver slipped 0.3% to $40.79 and Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) edged up 0.3% to $59,919. The CBOE Volatility Index eased to 27.6 after touching 34.95.

10 Tech Stocks Bouncing Off the Lows

The names hit hardest at the open led the recovery: AI infrastructure, memory and chip suppliers.

Read Also: 3 Things Every Bear Market in 50 Years Had in Common — Which One Is Missing Now?

Meanwhile, not everyone is buying the bounce.

“We are not out of the woods with the downside risk from the AI trade, as the Jensen Huang stock put is fading,” Chris Brigati, chief investment officer at SWBC, said in emailed comments. He expects the S&P 500 to dip close to 6,500 by year-end.

Jefferies equity strategist Steven DeSanctis sees the market’s breadth as the quieter story. “We have argued all year that we would see a broader equity market, thanks to earnings growth coming in better than average and more companies delivering over 20% earnings growth,” he said in a note Wednesday.

U.S. markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving and close early Friday at 1 p.m. ET. A single higher low does not make a bottom, but it gives the bulls their first line in the sand.

title: Billionaire Investor Made Meta a Top Bet Right Before Its AI Spending Shock
teaser: Billionaire Daniel Loeb's Third Point added Meta back in Q3 2026, making the stock its largest holding with 655,000 shares worth approximately $475 million.
body:
Hedge fund billionaire Daniel Loeb’s Third Point LLC rebuilt its stake in Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) in the third quarter and made it the fund’s largest reported holding, weeks before Meta’s spending and stock-sale plans sent the shares sliding.

Third Point reported 655,000 Meta shares worth about $475 million as of Sept. 30, according to its Form 13F. That made Meta the largest of the fund’s 39 reported holdings, at about 11% of its holdings excluding options.

The stake marks a return. Third Point held 90,000 Meta shares at the end of March and had sold all of them by the end of June, its filings show.

Read Also: Meta’s $25 Billion Headache: The ETF Cashing In on META’s Pain

The timing has put the bet under pressure. The holding’s $475 million value reflects Meta’s Sept. 30 close of $725.18. Three weeks later, Meta reported its first negative quarterly free cash flow since 2012, then laid out plans to raise about $95 billion by selling stock to fund its artificial intelligence buildout.

Loeb Swapped Amazon for Meta, Nvidia and Microsoft

Meta was part of a broader rotation inside Big Tech. Third Point also bought 1.5 million Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) shares worth $342.6 million and 450,000 Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ:MSFT) shares worth $230.8 million, while it sold out of Amazon.com Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) and cut its Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOGL) Class A stake 83% to 175,000 shares.

Nvidia was a return, too. Third Point held 190,000 Nvidia shares at the end of March before exiting in the second quarter.

A 13F shows only long U.S.-listed positions as of quarter-end and is filed up to 45 days later. It doesn’t show when Third Point bought, what it paid or whether it still owns the shares.

Why This Matters for Meta

Meta’s third-quarter results beat Wall Street estimates, with revenue of $64.6 billion against expectations of $63.37 billion and adjusted earnings of $7.40 per share against $5.74. But the company raised its full-year 2026 expense forecast to $175 billion to $179 billion from $165 billion to $169 billion, including a $9.9 billion legal charge, and guided capital spending to $135 billion to $145 billion.

That spending pushed free cash flow to negative $2.12 billion in the quarter, according to Meta’s earnings release, compared with $10.63 billion a year earlier.

On the Oct. 21 earnings call, CEO Mark Zuckerberg said Meta will be able to "build superintelligence through scaling." CFO Susan Li said the company will "continue investing aggressively" to support its core business and AI initiatives.

On Oct. 26, Meta announced plans to raise about $35 billion through stock offerings, plus a planned $60 billion at-the-market program to sell Class C shares that could start in the first quarter of 2027.

Third Point’s fourth-quarter 13F, due by mid-February, will show whether Loeb held Meta through the slide.

title: Disney Stock Hits 52-Week High: What's Happening?
teaser: Walt Disney shares are rising to a fresh 52-week high Wednesday, extending gains from last week's earnings report ESPN's Super Bowl momentum.
body:
The Walt Disney Co. (NYSE:DIS) shares are rising to a fresh 52-week high Wednesday. The company is seemingly building on last week’s earnings report as ESPN gets ready for the Super Bowl in February.

  • Walt Disney stock is approaching key resistance levels. Why are DIS shares at highs?

Disney Hits 52-Week High

The stock hit $125.17 on Wednesday, a new peak for the past 52 weeks, and it trades near $125.04. Coming into the session, the 52-week range ran from $92.19 to $123.37.

The chart backs the breakout. Disney is above its 20-day, 50-day and 200-day averages, and its 50-day average is higher than the 200-day. MACD reads 3.04, above both its 2.80 signal line and zero, which points to supportive momentum.

One caution: the shares are approximately 5.9% over their 20-day average of $118.06. A close under the former high of $123.37 would erase the breakout, and staying over the 20-day line would preserve the current pace.

Disney Sports Profit Jumps on NFL Deal

The rise is building on last week’s earnings. Sports operating income jumped 53% in the quarter, and Disney expects the game and the College Football Playoff calendar to lift Sports results in the fiscal second quarter.

CEO Josh D’Amaro said “live sports remain among the most powerful ways to bring fans together.” Disney credited stronger ad pricing, more affiliate revenue and its NFL equity stake, and said “Monday Night Football” had its best-ever Week 1 and Week 2 audiences.

For the entire fiscal year, Sports revenue grew 5% to $18.6 billion and operating income rose 7% to $3.1 billion.

ESPN will produce its first Super Bowl when Super Bowl LXI kicks off Feb. 14 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. ESPN and ABC will broadcast it, and Disney+ will stream it for U.S. subscribers.

DIS Shares Are Moving Higher

DIS Price Action: Walt Disney shares were up 2.01% at $124.97 at the time of publication on Wednesday. The stock is trading at a new 52-week high, according to Benzinga Pro.

author: Daragh Thomas
title: How Nvidia's Jensen Huang Survived the Kind of Scandal That Ends CEO Careers
teaser: Jensen Huang survived the kind of scandal that ended CEO careers at McDonald’s, BP and Intel.
body:
Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang got his job back on Monday after resigning amid reports of undisclosed relationships with employees.

Other CEOs haven’t been so fortunate. Similar scandals have ended careers at McDonald’s, BP and Intel, costing some executives tens of millions of dollars in compensation.

When Office Romances End Careers

McDonald’s (NYSE:MCD) fired Steve Easterbrook in 2019 over a consensual relationship with an employee. After discovering additional undisclosed relationships, the company sued Easterbrook and recovered more than $105 million in cash and equity awards.

In 2023, BP (NYSE:BP) CEO Bernard Looney resigned after failing to fully disclose relationships with colleagues. The oil giant concluded that Looney had knowingly misled its board, costing him up to £32.4 million (about $41 million) in compensation.

Even Nvidia’s own industry has a precedent. Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) then-CEO Brian Krzanich resigned in 2018 after an investigation found that a consensual relationship with an employee violated company policy.

The Rules He Helped Write

Separate from the national security concerns surrounding Huang’s resignation, The New York Times reported on Nov. 11 that he had a relationship with Nvidia’s healthcare vice president, Kimberly Powell, who reported directly to him.

At Tuesday’s employee meeting, Huang acknowledged violating company policies and said he had written much of Nvidia’s code of conduct himself. He argued that a breach should not automatically lead to dismissal, WIRED reported.

“It has to always be evaluated in the context of the human,” Huang said.

Wall Street’s Trillion-Dollar Exception

Nvidia shares lost nearly a third of their value after the scandal broke. Monday’s rally added back nearly $1 trillion in market value, though the stock was still down 17% from its pre-scandal price as of Tuesday’s close.

The wider AI industry relies on Nvidia for both chips and financing, and investors had feared Huang’s departure could disrupt it. Even Jay Goldberg, a Seaport Research Partners analyst and longtime Nvidia bear, put it bluntly.

“There’s no one that can really replace Jensen. I mean, he does the roles of like several people,” he previously told Benzinga.

Who Pays the Price?

In July last year, Astronomer CEO Andy Byron and human resources chief Kristin Cabot both resigned after a camera caught them embracing at a Coldplay concert.

Byron landed another executive role this month, while Cabot has yet to find another job, Bloomberg reported.

At Nvidia, Huang is already back in charge, but prediction market traders are less confident about the future of Powell, the executive with whom he reportedly had a relationship.

Traders on Polymarket put the odds of Powell resigning or being removed by year-end at 23%, compared with just 5.1% for Huang.

In other words, traders think Powell is more than four times as likely as her boss to lose or leave her position at Nvidia by the end of the year.
